decisions.question: q-316607

authoring.question: q-316607
authoring.value:
First, let's sketch our region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13992537/assets/059560835586e9c149cdb5dabcddc80610a58bfa0c30cb5f685b8bb6bdca3e90.png)

Recall that for any linear transformation $T,$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $T(D)$ under the action of $T:$

$$
\text{Area}(T(D))=|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D).
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D)=\frac{1}{2}\cdot 6\cdot 5=15.
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$
det(T)=2\cdot 2-0\cdot 0=4.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|\,4\,|\cdot 15 \\  & =60.\end{aligned}
$$

decisions.question: e-5471

authoring.question: e-5471
authoring.value:
First, let's sketch our region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13992537/assets/ee8f0cf16983d87fa505303ed6372a3f389518d05b3e13f2e9e2121038792b84.png)

Recall that for any linear transformation $\mathbf{T},$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $\mathbf{T}(D)$ under the action of $\mathbf{T}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\text{Area}(\mathbf{T}(D)) = |\det(T)| \cdot \text{Area}(D)
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D) = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot 3 \cdot 4 = 6.
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$
\det(T) = (-7) \cdot 3 -  5 \cdot (-2) = -11.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|-11|\cdot 6 \\  & =66.\end{aligned}
$$
